impact.description: 1st place at the MSOE AI Club Hacksgiving hackathon

case_study.context: The Milwaukee Domes Alliance wanted to increase visitor engagement and revenue while supporting its upcoming renovation. Our team developed a concept during a 50-hour MSOE AI Club Hacksgiving hackathon.
case_study.my_role: UX product designer and researcher; presenter.

action.action_description: Interviewed the CEO and education director, reviewed the current website and planned changes, and identified visitor use cases and opportunities to support the Domes.
Sketched ideas in Microsoft Whiteboard and prototyped an AI-powered visitor experience in Figma, including Botanical Tales, Sip & Seek tours, and the Dome Detectives photo scavenger hunt.
Field-tested the interactive concept at the Domes, handed it off to software engineers for implementation, and prepared and presented a proposal to stakeholders and judges.

case_study.result: Field testing showed the concept worked as intended and was entertaining and informative for visitors. The team won first place in the Hacksgiving hackathon.
case_study.summary: Prototyped and field-tested an AI-powered visitor experience designed to support engagement and revenue at the Milwaukee Domes Alliance.

impact.description: less configuration time through my workflow redesigns

case_study.context: L & S Electric needed a modern desktop app for configuring and controlling its AES-110 and AES-1100 hydro-electric power excitation systems. The users are electrical engineers and field technicians (both inside and outside of L & S Electric, Inc.) working live with power generation equipment, where a misread value or mis-click has drastic consequences. The app had to combine real-time metering, a multi-channel oscilloscope, COMTRADE fault-file analysis, synchroscope and capability curve displays, and automated control sequences.
case_study.my_role: Lead User Experience Designer, Researcher, and Writer

action.action_description: I ran working sessions with L & S electrical engineers to understand how they commission, tune, and troubleshoot excitation systems, and which readings they need side by side during each task. I also shadowed a technician through a commissioning workflow on the legacy tool.

I organized screens into task-based modes (configuration, monitoring, control, fault analysis) so engineers could move between them without losing context. A/B testing with 4 to 5 engineers shaped the navigation.

I designed the auto-control and sequence screens with clear state indicators, confirmation steps for irreversible commands, and consistent placement of critical readings while making sure to follow L & S's own accessibility and HMI standards.
I designed the oscilloscope and COMTRADE views — channel toggles, zoom bands, and RMS/frequency/phase measurement readouts — so engineers could isolate a fault window quickly.
I created a reusable component library (gauges, metering tiles, alarm states) that let development scale consistently.

I reviewed builds with engineers each iteration and refined layouts based on what they actually looked for first, conducting usability walkthroughs at roughly every two to four weeks. I also experimented with field testing during QA testing for AES-110s.

case_study.result: One unified, scalable tool replaced several outdated tools for configuring, monitoring, and analyzing excitation systems. Configuration time decreased by about 50%. Engineers can analyze historical fault events in the same oscilloscope interface they use live, shortening root-cause analysis from hours to minutes. Consistent patterns across all pages reduce training time for new technicians and lower the risk of operator error on live equipment. The product gives L & S a modern, branded software experience to pair with their hardware in customer sales.

impact.description: 2nd place in the MSOE AI Club Discovery World hackathon

case_study.context: Discovery World wanted a cost-effective, technology-based way to improve exhibit accessibility. During a 50-hour MSOE AI Club hackathon, our team explored a solution designed to require little effort from visitors.
case_study.my_role: UX researcher and designer; presentation creator.

action.action_description: Visited Discovery World to observe and test existing accessibility tools, consulted stakeholders, and identified visitor needs and underrepresented groups the concept could serve.
Sketched and wireframed a low-cost concept, then prototyped a chatbot that uses Bluetooth repeaters to locate visitors and tailor exhibit information to different ages.
Documented the design process in a presentation and handed the prototype to software engineers for implementation.

case_study.result: The team earned second place with a seamless, cost-effective accessibility concept that was easy to implement and required little to no effort from visitors.
case_study.summary: Designed an accessible, age-aware exhibit chatbot for Discovery World with the MSOE AI Club.

impact.description: High-fidelity prototype refined through peer feedback and material testing

case_study.context: For a 14-week industrial design project, I set out to take a sustainable physical product from initial research through a high-fidelity prototype ready for theoretical publication.

action.action_description: Completed field and competitive research, sketched early concepts, refined the design digitally, and built a rough clay model.
Created 3D models in SolidWorks and Autodesk Fusion 360, inverted the product design into a mold, and 3D-printed the mold.
Collected feedback from peers and professors, tested materials, identified design issues, and refined the product through repeated experiments, including work with flexible TPU molds.

case_study.result: Created a high-fidelity prototype of a hand-soap bottle made from recycled hotel soaps with a one-time-use pump. After the liquid soap is used, the outer bottle can be used as soap, avoiding a discarded plastic bottle.
case_study.summary: Designed and prototyped a hand-soap bottle made from recycled hotel soaps, with an outer bottle that can be used as soap after the liquid is gone.
